title: Heat
content: Heat is the form of energy that can be transferred from one system to another as a result of temperature difference.
e: Heat is energy on the move between systems because their temperatures differ. It is not a fluid stored inside a body. When the two temperatures match, net heat flow drops to zero.

title: Heat conduction
content: Heat conduction is one mode of energy transfer. The individual parts of a medium do not move as a whole in heat conduction. Heat energy is transferred by successive distribution among the adjacent parts in heat conduction.
e: Conduction passes thermal energy through vibrating atoms and molecules while the bulk of the material stays put. Neighbours share energy in turn. Fluids can also conduct, but this mode does not rely on the material flowing as a whole.

title: Thermal conductivity
content: Thermal conductivity of the material is a measure of the ability of a material to conduct heat.
e: Thermal conductivity k tells you how readily a material carries heat for a given temperature gradient. A large k means a thermal conductor. A small k means a thermal insulator, with SI unit watt per metre per kelvin.

title: Heat Convection
content: Heat convection is the flow of heat through a fluid from places of higher temperature to places of lower temperature by movement of the fluid itself.
e: Convection is heat carried by the fluid itself as hot, less dense fluid rises and cooler fluid sinks. That bulk motion is the point. A rigid solid cannot set up convection currents.

title: Heat Radiation
content: Heat radiation is a transfer of heat that does not require a material medium. Heat is transferred by thermal radiation which are electromagnetic waves that pass through a medium or even vacuum.
e: Radiation sends heat as electromagnetic waves, so no material medium is required. The waves can even cross vacuum at the speed of light. That is how the Sun warms the Earth.

title: Blackbody
content: The object which can absorb all the electromagnetic radiations falling upon it is called a blackbody.
e: A blackbody absorbs every electromagnetic wave that hits it. Because a perfect absorber is also a perfect emitter, its emissivity is taken as 1. A shiny reflector is the opposite kind of surface.

title: Blackbody radiation
content: The radiation emitted by a blackbody is called blackbody radiation.
e: Blackbody radiation is the spectrum a blackbody emits. The shape and the power of that spectrum depend on absolute temperature. Real surfaces emit less than this ideal at the same temperature.

title: Total emissive power
content: The total emissive power is defined as the total radiant energy of different wavelengths emitted from unit area of a surface of a body in one second.
e: Total emissive power is the radiant energy of all wavelengths leaving unit area of a surface in one second. It measures how strongly the surface radiates. Stefan-Boltzmann's law then links that power to temperature for a blackbody.

title: Stefan - Boltzmann's Law
content: The total emissive power of a blackbody is directly proportional to the fourth power of absolute temperature.
e: Stefan-Boltzmann's law says a blackbody's total emissive power grows with the fourth power of absolute temperature. The equation is e0 = sigma T^4. A small change in kelvin therefore changes the radiated power a lot.

title: Emissivity
content: Emissivity is defined as the ratio of the total emissive power of an object to that of the blackbody, at the same temperature and wavelength.
e: Emissivity is the ratio of an object's total emissive power to that of a blackbody at the same temperature and wavelength. A dull black surface sits near 1. A polished silver surface sits far below 1.

title: Thermodynamics
content: Thermodynamics is the study of systems involving energy in the form of heat and work.
e: Thermodynamics studies systems whose energy shows up as heat and as work. It maps equilibrium states and how you move between them. Heat transfer then asks how energy actually flows while those states change.

title: The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics
content: When two objects are separately in thermodynamic equilibrium with a third object, they all are in thermodynamics equilibrium with each other.
e: Zeroth law says if A and B are each in thermodynamic equilibrium with a third body C, then A and B are in equilibrium with each other. That shared equilibrium is what lets a thermometer define temperature. A fourth body is not required.

title: First Law of Thermodynamics
content: The change in internal energy ΔU of a system is equal to the net heat flow Q into the system minus the total work W done by the system.
e: First law is energy conservation for heat and work: the change in internal energy equals heat added minus work done by the system. Q is positive when heat enters. W is positive when the system does the work.

title: Internal Energy
content: The internal energy U of a system is defined as the sum of the energies of all constituent particles.
e: Internal energy U is the total energy of all particles that make up the system. For an ideal gas it depends only on absolute temperature. Heat and work can change U, but they are not stored as heat or work inside the system.

title: Thermodynamics process
content: A thermodynamics process may be defined as a change from one equilibrium state of a system to another.
e: A thermodynamic process is a change from one equilibrium state to another. If you crawl slowly enough, the system stays internally in equilibrium and the process is quasi-static. Fast, violent jumps leave you off that path.

title: Heat engine
content: Heat engine is a system that converts heat to mechanical energy, which can be used to do mechanical work.
e: A heat engine takes heat from a hot source and turns part of it into mechanical work. The leftover heat is dumped to a colder sink. You then repeat the same cycle so work keeps coming out.

title: Thermal efficiency
content: Thermal efficiency for a heat engine is the ratio of work output to heat input.
e: Thermal efficiency is work output divided by heat input. For a full cycle Delta U is zero, so W equals Q_H minus Q_C, and eta is also 1 minus Q_C over Q_H. A bigger dump of heat to the cold side lowers the efficiency.

title: Carnot's Theorem
content: Carnot's theorem states that no engine operating between two heat reservoirs can be more efficient than a Carnot's engine operating between the same heat reservoirs.
e: Carnot's theorem says no engine working between two reservoirs can beat a Carnot engine between those same reservoirs. Every reversible engine on that pair of reservoirs shares the same efficiency. Real engines fall short because of irreversibility and friction.
